1.constraint: Use this terracotta linen-like half-button hooded pullover once only for Spring, mild-Fall or cool-Summer Casual Everyday, Weekend, Travel, Resort evening or a relaxed daytime Date. Pair with one controlled straight or tailored bottom in ecru, stone, charcoal, chocolate or muted olive and a cream, tan or tobacco shoe; avoid another hood, loose drawstring bottom, bulky sneaker or all-brown styling.

6.constraint: Use this apricot notched linen-like long-sleeve shirt once only for Spring/Summer Resort, Vacation, Travel, Casual Everyday, creative Office or a daytime Date. Pair with a straight trouser or tailored short in charcoal, chocolate, tobacco, stone or muted olive and a cream, tan or brown low-profile shoe; keep the neckline polished and do not add an oversized bottom, second loose shirt layer or loud print.

13.constraint: Use this saturated peacock-blue waffle half-zip hoodie once only for Fall/Winter Casual Everyday, Weekend, Campus, Travel or a deliberate daytime Party look. Balance it with one controlled straight bottom in ecru, stone, charcoal, cocoa or deep olive and an off-white, tan or gray low-profile shoe; never pair it with baggy jeans, another bright blue garment, a technical running shoe or a dark monotone coat.

23.constraint: Use this washed-blue relaxed-tapered cropped jean once only for Spring/Summer Casual Everyday, Weekend, Travel, Campus or a relaxed daytime Date. Pair with a regular-fit or lightly relaxed top in cream, terracotta, sage, dusty pink or warm navy and a low-profile cream, tan or brown shoe; keep the single rolled hem clean and never add an oversized top, chunky sneaker, distressed layer or second washed-denim statement.

rejectionGroups.reason: The synthetic half-button shirt is visually near-duplicate to the mint summer henley already accepted in batch 26, so another recolored version would add identity without useful style diversity.
The flax half-button shirt is narrow and elongated through the torso with a deep-open neckline, repeating the rejected skinny resort-top problem.
These product-only hoodies provide no adult shoulder, torso, sleeve or hem proof and repeat already reviewed basic hoodie roles.
The lace-up short-sleeve top is visibly tight through the chest, waist and arms and uses a dated costume-like neckline.
The pastel leaf-print shirt is product-only, busy and unproven on an adult body; a soft palette does not rescue weak fit proof and novelty repetition.
These product-only long-sleeve henley or crew tops have visibly narrow elongated bodies and no trustworthy adult fit proof.
The cap-sleeve tank and deep-V pocket tee are body-hugging, arm- and chest-emphasizing tops rather than versatile modern layers.
These product-only short-sleeve T-shirts use boxy oversized outlines and provide no adult drape or proportion proof across their recolors.
The product-only lace-up long blouse is overlong, theatrical and costume-led, with no credible general outfit role.
These wide, loose, flared or contrast-panel jeans and pants carry excessive leg volume, visible shoe pooling or distorted dark washes, directly repeating the rejected baggy-bottom problem.
The black technical joggers are extremely wide through the thigh and lower leg, cuff-bunched and styled with a bulky performance sneaker.
The bright bohemian harem pants combine ballooned volume, a dropped shape and loud novelty print rather than controlled modern proportion.
These product-only winter coats and puffers are repetitive, bulky or utility-heavy, with faux-fur, shiny shells, visible pseudo-brand details, dark repetition or no adult fit and movement proof.
The banquet suit is explicitly wedding-styled, uses a tight artificial-looking cut and loud recolors, and remains outside the non-wedding scope.
